The scalar assigned to a closed spacetime manifold by a topological quantum field theory. Gluing the two ends of a cylinder over a spatial manifold Σ gives Z(Σ×S1)=tr(1V(Σ)​)=dimV(Σ). Vacuum state (∣0⟩)

Words: 78
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
For a stable relativistic quantum field theory in Minkowski space, a vacuum is a lowest-energy state for the chosen time evolution; a physical vacuum is normally also invariant under spacetime translations. It need not have zero fluctuations or vanish under every field operator. A free field's Fock vacuum is annihilated by its annihilation operators, while an interacting vacuum need not equal the free-theory Fock state. Multiple degenerate vacua permit spontaneous symmetry breaking. In curved spacetime the choice of time evolution and positive-frequency modes introduces additional vacuum ambiguity in a nonstationary spacetime.

Quantum field (Φ(x))

Words: 144 Articles: 2
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A quantum field is an operator-valued distribution on spacetime: smearing Φ(x) against a smooth test function gives an operator, whereas pointwise products can require renormalization. For example, a free complex scalar field contains particle annihilation operators and antiparticle creation operators. Its microcausality condition makes field commutators vanish at spacelike separation. For fermions, the corresponding locality condition uses anticommutators. This combines quantum operators with the spacetime locality of a quantum field theory.

Taking a matrix element between momentum eigenstates gives ⟨q∣Φ(x)∣p⟩=ei(q−p)⋅x⟨q∣Φ(0)∣p⟩. Differentiating gives i∂t​Φ=[Φ,H] and −i∇Φ=[Φ,P], connecting the Heisenberg equation of motion to spatial translation covariance.

For p2=m2>0, let a unitary operator U implement a Lorentz boost taking p to (m,0). For a Lorentz scalar field, ⟨q∣ϕ(x)∣p⟩=⟨Ψ∣ϕ(0)∣m,0⟩ with ∣Ψ⟩=e−i(q−p)⋅xU∣q⟩. The phase follows from translation covariance of a quantum field; its complex conjugate enters the bra. The transformed energy eigenvalue is (Λq)0=p⋅q/m by invariance of the Minkowski inner product. Algebraic quantum field theory

Words: 281 Articles: 3
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
Algebraic quantum field theory assigns an observable algebra A(O) to each suitable spacetime region O. Inclusion of regions implies inclusion of algebras, and spacelike-separated algebras commute under microcausality. A state is a positive normalized functional on the observable algebra, so its restriction to a region specifies expectation values and correlations for that algebra. Spectrum conditions restrict translation representations, while primitive causality and time-slice axioms constrain the dynamics; these are different assumptions.

Time-slice axiom

Words: 76
Algebraic quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
The time-slice axiom says that an algebra generated in an arbitrarily thin suitable neighbourhood of a Cauchy surface generates the algebra of its causal development. For O such a neighbourhood in its development D(O), this is A(O)=A(D(O)). Precise global and local versions can differ in the regions to which they apply. For a local hyperbolic field equation, later fields can be represented using the initial field and its conjugate momentum in the corresponding domain of dependence.

Primitive causality

Words: 74
Algebraic quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
Primitive causality is a dynamical completeness condition: the state restricted to a suitable initial spacetime region determines its expectations throughout that region's domain of dependence. Algebraically one requires the later domain-of-dependence observable algebra to be contained in the initial algebra, under the identifications supplied by the dynamics. A local time-slice axiom gives this property for a neighbourhood of a Cauchy slice. Knowledge of the full restricted state, including correlations, is required; knowing only mean initial fields is insufficient.

Spectrum condition (Sp(P)⊆V+​)

Words: 68
Algebraic quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
In a translation-covariant quantum field theory on Minkowski spacetime, the joint spectrum of the energy-momentum generators is required to lie in the closed future light cone. With signature (+,−,−,−) this means p0≥0 and p2≥0. The spectrum condition implements a positive-energy stability requirement in every inertial frame. It constrains the Fourier support and analyticity of vacuum correlation functions but does not by itself assert spacelike commutation or an initial-value property.

Positive-energy spectrum condition (specPμ⊆V+​)

Words: 44
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
The joint energy-momentum spectrum lies in the closed forward light cone. In axiomatic quantum field theory, this condition permits analytic continuation of Wightman functions in suitable complex spacetime domains. Together with Lorentz invariance, microcausality and the positivity of the physical state space, it is one of the hypotheses behind the CPT theorem.

Canonical transformation of mode operators (ai′​=∑j​(Uij​aj​+Vij​aj†​))

Words: 1k Articles: 28
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A linear change of creation operators and annihilation operators is canonical when it preserves their defining brackets. For finitely many bosonic modes, the canonical commutation relations require UU†−VV†=I and UVT−VUT=0. For fermions, the canonical anticommutation relations instead require UU†+VV†=I and UVT+VUT=0. A Bogoliubov transformation uses such mixing to diagonalize a quadratic Hamiltonian or relate different vacuum descriptions. Infinite-mode unitary implementation has further conditions, as in bosonic mode mixing implementability.

Bogoliubov transformation

Words: 1k Articles: 27
Canonical transformation of mode operators OurBigBook.com
A Bogoliubov transformation is a canonical transformation of mode operators mixing creation operators and annihilation operators. It diagonalizes quadratic Hamiltonians or relates different vacuum descriptions. Bosonic and fermionic canonical bracket constraints differ. A nonzero creation-mixing coefficient makes its vacuum contain particles relative to the original mode decomposition.

If ak​=uk​bk​−vk​b−k†​, its original-mode occupation number is ∣vk​∣2. It is generally a multimode squeezed vacuum rather than the original Fock vacuum. In infinitely many modes, existence in the original Fock space requires a separate convergence analysis.

Real-angle unitarity within each two-by-two block alone does not enforce consistency between duplicated momentum labels.

An effective Lagrangian encodes the interactions of retained degrees of freedom after others have been removed, often by a path integral. For external energies below a massive field's excitation threshold, its effects admit a local expansion in external momenta divided by its mass. Matching scattering amplitudes fixes the coefficients of the resulting local operators; truncation has a specified order in that small ratio.

An effective operator is a local interaction built from the retained fields in an effective field theory. In four dimensions an operator of mass dimension Δi​ has the displayed coefficient for dimensionless Ci​ and a heavy mass scale M. For example a dimension-six proton-decay operator has a coefficient proportional to M−2.

A low-energy effective action retains the light degrees of freedom and describes the effects of heavier ones through local interactions and a derivative expansion. It can be obtained by matching an effective field theory or by a low-energy compactification. A Wilsonian effective action implements integration of high-energy modes with a scale cutoff. The quantum effective action that generates one-particle-irreducible vertices is a different construction; the two need not coincide.

An operator basis in effective field theory is an independent set of allowed local field operators at a chosen order, modulo relevant algebraic identities, integration by parts and permitted field redefinitions. An infrared regulator suppresses the small-momentum region responsible for an infrared divergence. Examples are a small positive mass or a finite volume. It must be distinguished from an ultraviolet cutoff: setting external momenta and masses to zero to extract an ultraviolet divergence can introduce a spurious infrared divergence. Keep a positive auxiliary mass until the divergent local coefficients have been separated, then take the desired limit in infrared-safe quantities.

Words: 49
Infrared divergence OurBigBook.com
An observable unchanged by adding a particle with vanishing energy or replacing one massless particle by exactly collinear particles with the same total momentum. This property permits cancellation of real and virtual infrared divergences and collinear divergences in its perturbative cross-section. Fully inclusive electron-positron hadronic rates and suitably defined jet observables are examples.

A singularity of a massless scattering or radiation integral when momenta of two particles become parallel. In Quantum chromodynamics, unresolved quark-gluon splittings cause such divergences. A mass regulator or dimensional regularization exposes them; they cancel between suitable inclusive real and virtual contributions or are absorbed into factorized distributions where appropriate.

Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
A quantum field theory has a mass gap when the vacuum energy is separated from the rest of the spectrum by a strictly positive energy. Correlation functions then typically decay exponentially at long distance.

Spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB)

Words: 4k Articles: 44
Quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
Spontaneous symmetry breaking occurs when the action and equations have a symmetry but a chosen ground state is invariant only under a proper subgroup. Acting with the broken symmetry generates a degenerate vacuum manifold. An order parameter distinguishes the selected states: the equations do not prefer its direction, yet a particular state does. This lets one use the symmetry of the laws to predict excitations around a state that has less symmetry, notably the Goldstone bosons of a broken continuous symmetry.
A finite system with symmetry-preserving boundary conditions can have a symmetric ground state; a symmetric statistical mixture of broken states also has vanishing mean order parameter. A nonzero mean therefore requires a stated selection procedure. The symmetry-breaking order of limits takes the thermodynamic limit in a small applied source before removing that source. The finite-volume angular source selection example makes the distinction explicit for a continuous symmetry.

The usual bound of three distinct eigenvalues requires this polynomial not to vanish identically. With b=0, a,m>0, every traceless matrix of squared norm R2=m2/(2a) is a global minimum, including matrices with all eigenvalues distinct. In SU(5), this permits an unbroken maximal torus U(1)4, outside the generic three-block classification.

Every v∈VH has H⊆Stab(v); equality requires a separate stabilizer calculation. The criterion neither determines the full unbroken group nor guarantees that a given scalar potential has its minimum at that direction.

Indeed, eiθ preserves every condensate if and only if eiQi​θ=1 for every i. The Bezout identity implies eidθ=1, and conversely d∣Qi​ proves every dth root of unity preserves every condensate. Its identity component is ∏i​SO(mi​). Thus a scalar multiple of the identity preserves the whole group, whereas a tensor with simple spectrum preserves only diagonal signs with total sign one. A tracelessness condition constrains the eigenvalues but does not change this stabilizer formula.

Nambu superconductivity and chiral symmetry analogy

Words: 441
Spontaneous symmetry breaking OurBigBook.com
Yoichiro Nambu's superconductivity work led to the spontaneous symmetry breaking ideas recognized by his share of the 2008 Nobel Prize in Physics.[ref] His 1960 treatment made the Meissner effect response consistent with gauge invariance by including collective pair contributions alongside the quasiparticles. The resulting Ward identity relates the interaction correction to the current and the self-energy; retaining the quasiparticles alone omits part of the response.[ref]
The individual Nobel lecture explains the bridge to physics: the superconductivity gap suggested a dynamically generated fermion mass, and the accompanying collective excitation suggested a light pion. It also notes that the long-range Coulomb interaction turns the charged phase response into a plasmon. A neutral global phase mode and a charged material therefore need different low-momentum descriptions.[ref]
In 1961, Yoichiro Nambu and Giovanni Jona-Lasinio supplied a four-fermion model with a self-consistent mass and a massless pseudoscalar bound state: an idealized pion. Their original constituents were nucleon fields. Their introduction explicitly distinguishes the zero-mass neutral collective excitation from its charged plasma counterpart and allows approximate chiral symmetry as the explanation of a nonzero pion mass. This is a model of dynamical symmetry breaking, rather than a microscopic derivation of Quantum chromodynamics.[ref]
In the modern two-light-quark account, chiral symmetry breaking leaves isospin intact and produces three Goldstone bosons in the exact non-anomalous chiral limit. Small quark masses explicitly break that chiral symmetry, so the observed pions are pseudo-Goldstone bosons. The chiral protection of a fermion mass identifies the distinct obstruction to inserting an explicit fermion mass into a chirally symmetric equation. The useful lesson is that massive individual excitations and much lighter collective excitations can coexist because they describe different motions of an interacting state.
A concrete experimental motivation for treating the electromagnetic response carefully is the Field-cooled Meissner experiment. MIT's realization cools lead in a solenoid field using helium gas. A nearby thermometer follows the cooling; a test coil feeds an integrator and oscilloscope. Expulsion gives a pulse, warming reverses it, and switching off the field while the sample is normal checks its sign. A change in alternating-field response alone can reflect normal electrical conductivity. This readout tests magnetic flux expulsion, not the spectrum or existence of a neutral Goldstone boson.[ref]
For a global symmetry in field theory, different orientations can be physically distinct states. A local gauge symmetry instead includes redundant descriptions of the same physical state. A gauge-dependent field expectation alone is consequently insufficient as a physical criterion for spontaneous symmetry breaking. The Higgs mechanism changes the physical mode content when the gauge field is dynamical; the global Goldstone theorem alone does not prove that mechanism. In particular, the massless direction of a gauge-fixed scalar potential need not appear as a separately observable massless particle.

The two signs are related by the symmetry, although the individual pure vacua are not invariant under it.

Goldstone theorem

Words: 637 Articles: 6
Spontaneous symmetry breaking OurBigBook.com
In a local quantum field theory obeying special relativity, with a positive physical state space, a conserved continuous internal global symmetry in field theory and a selected Lorentz-invariant ground state, a broken generator requires a massless Goldstone boson. For G→H, there are dimG−dimH symmetry-required Goldstone bosons in this setting; additional accidental massless excitations are possible. Jeffrey Goldstone's institutional biography identifies his work with Abdus Salam and Steven Weinberg on the zero-mass theorem.[ref]
The Goldstone directions in the scalar mass matrix give a short classical proof at a smooth minimum. The quantum argument uses a conserved current jμ and a scalar local operator O whose expectation changes under the broken generator. The Ward identity for the current–local operator correlation function then has a nonzero contact term. After a Fourier transform, its divergence remains nonzero as four-momentum tends to zero. Lorentz invariance forces the vector–scalar correlator to have the form pμF(p2), so F must have a pole at p2=0. The spectral representation associates that pole with a physical zero-mass excitation. A properly regulated spatial integral of the conserved current implements the broken generator; a well-defined global charge acting on the broken ground state cannot simply be assumed.
The hypotheses explain the boundaries of the result. A discrete symmetry has no infinitesimal generator and need not give a Goldstone boson. A gauge redundancy does not supply the physical global generator assumed here. In nonrelativistic matter the type-B Goldstone boson shows why one cannot universally count one independent mode per broken generator. Long-wavelength fluctuations can also prevent an assumed broken state from existing, as in the Mermin-Wagner theorem.

CP violation

Words: 1k Articles: 12
Discrete symmetry in quantum field theory OurBigBook.com
CP violation is the failure of a theory to be invariant under the combination of charge conjugation and parity. Under CPT invariance it is equivalent to time-reversal violation.
CP violation matters experimentally because a symmetry predicts a forbidden transition, not merely a small correction to a permitted one. The Christenson-Cronin-Fitch-Turlay kaon CP violation experiment found evidence for precisely such a transition: a long-lived neutral kaon decaying into two pions. Understanding that inference requires both two-pion kaon event reconstruction and the distinction between kaon CP eigenstates and the physical states of neutral kaon mixing.

Christenson-Cronin-Fitch-Turlay kaon CP violation experiment

Words: 213
CP violation OurBigBook.com
James H. Christenson, James Watson Cronin, Val Logsdon Fitch and René Turlay reported the result in 1964. At Brookhaven's AGS, 30 GeV protons struck beryllium; collimators selected a neutral particle beam at 30 degrees. A downstream helium decay volume reduced interactions.[ref]
The flight distance suppressed the short-lived kaon component. Each arm of a two-arm magnetic spectrometer had spark chambers before and after its magnet. Cherenkov detectors and scintillation counters triggered photographic recording in coincidence.[ref]
The helium sample yielded 45±9 signal events; (2.0±0.4)×10−3 was the ratio to all charged decay channels.[ref] That denominator must be retained when comparing this result with a total branching fraction.
The evidence was kinematic. Later regenerated-beam quantum interference established that the short- and long-lived states reached the same two-pion final state, excluding alternatives such as distinct pion-like particles.[ref] The 1964 observation established evidence for CP violation; it did not determine every parameter of the CKM matrix. Inferring time-reversal symmetry violation from CP violation invokes CPT symmetry, rather than a direct comparison of time-reversed transitions in that experiment.

E±​=p±2​+mπ2​​,Mππ2​=2mπ2​+2(E+​E−​−p+​p−​cosα).
(12)
This follows by expanding the squared sum of the two four-momenta. The angle θ between the reconstructed parent momentum P=p+​+p−​ and the neutral particle beam direction n^ satisfies
cosθ=∣P∣P⋅n^​.
(13)
A fully reconstructed two-body decay channel gives the parent mass and θ≃0, within experimental resolution. A three-body decay channel with an unseen neutrino generally misses both constraints; an accidental correct invariant mass alone is insufficient. Notice that the track opening angle α need not be small even when the parent direction angle θ vanishes.
The 1964 analysis selected 490<Mππ​<510 MeV and remeasured events with cosθ>0.9995, comparing adjacent mass bands.[ref]
For an original dimensionless example, take mπ​=1, n^=(0,0,1) and p±​=(±3​,0,3). Each energy is 13​; the opening angle is 60 degrees since cosα=(9−3)/(9+3)=1/2. Yet P=(0,0,6) points exactly along the beam, and Mππ2​=4(13)−36=16. Thus a parent of mass 4 passes both ideal tests. These chosen numbers illustrate four-momentum conservation, not detector performance.

Different forward scattering amplitudes, including absorption, can therefore generate a two-pion signal even with CP symmetry. Ordinary matter is not a CP-symmetric preparation.
Tungsten regeneration calibrated the signal; scanning its position sampled acceptance. Helium regeneration was insufficient, bag walls lay outside acceptance, vertex distributions excluded collimator regeneration, and hydrogen data cross-checked the effect.[ref] These controls are central: the question is whether the long-lived component itself reaches two pions, rather than whether material has prepared a fresh short-lived component.

The CPT theorem states that every local Lorentz-invariant quantum field theory with a Hermitian Hamiltonian is invariant under the combined action of charge conjugation, parity and time reversal. An operator that is odd under CP must therefore also be odd under time reversal if CPT is preserved.

It does not force equality of every pair of conjugate partial decay widths when CP violation is present.

A Lorentz scalar contracts all such indices, so the total sign is positive; charged terms are exchanged with their Hermitian conjugates. Therefore a local Hermitian Lagrangian density obeys ΘL(x)Θ−1=L(−x), leaving its action invariant. This field-level argument illustrates the CPT theorem for ordinary scalar, spinor and vector theories; the axiomatic theorem also uses positive energy and microcausality.

The arbitrary center t0​ supplies a translation zero mode, treated as a collective coordinate in the instanton fluctuation prefactor.
Even and odd instanton sums in a double well
Words: 31
Quartic double-well instanton OurBigBook.com
Return amplitudes sum even numbers of well-to-well events, while transfer amplitudes sum odd numbers. A dilute event gas gives cosh and sinh factors and a doublet splitting 2ℏAe−S0​/ℏ.
Quartic double-well fluctuation determinant (det′LI​/detL0​=1/(12ω2))
Words: 44
Quartic double-well instanton OurBigBook.com
The quartic double-well instanton has LI​=−∂τ2​+ω2[1−3sech2(ωτ/2)/2]. For a positive regulator ε and r=21+ε/ω2​, the common infinite-line determinant ratio is (r−1)(r−2)/[(r+1)(r+2)]. Its zero-mode factor is ε/(12ω2) to leading order, giving the displayed primed ratio. Therefore the instanton fluctuation prefactor is K=ω6SI​/(πℏ)​ and the double-well tunneling splitting is 2ℏKe−SI​/ℏ.

Operator-path-integral equivalence

Words: 62
Path integral OurBigBook.com
With a time-slice regulator, inserting field-coordinate resolutions of identity in evolution kernels produces a bosonic phase-space path integral; integrating the canonical momentum gives the configuration-space action. For fermions, resolutions in fermionic coherent states instead produce a Berezin integral and the first-order kinetic term. Vacuum endpoint projection supplies the Feynman i-epsilon prescription. Both constructions reproduce the same free oscillator correlators and their Wick theorem expansions, and thus agree order by order in a regulated perturbation series.

Euclidean worldline path integral

Words: 136 Articles: 1
Path integral OurBigBook.com
A thermal path integral represents the canonical partition function by paths periodic in Euclidean time of circumference β. For H=p2/2+V(x), its formal action is SE​[x]=∫0β​(x˙2/2+V(x))dτ. The periodic boundary condition results from taking the trace of the evolution kernel. The continuum measure requires a regularization and normalization; finite-dimensional measures make both choices explicit.

Fourier-cutoff oscillator functional determinant (ZN​=AN​ω−1∏r=1N​(ω2+νr2​)−1)

Words: 88
Euclidean worldline path integral OurBigBook.com
Use an orthonormal real Fourier series basis on a circle of length β, with νr​=2πr/β. Retain the constant coefficient and the sine/cosine pair for each 1≤r≤N. The oscillator action becomes 21​ω2q02​+21​∑r​(ω2+νr2​)(qr2​+sr2​). A product of real Gaussian integrals gives the displayed functional determinant, with AN​ independent of ω. Ratios for two frequencies converge regardless of AN​. The absolute limit requires its normalization: AN​=β−1∏r​νr2​ gives the thermal partition function of a quantum harmonic oscillator in the limit. Multiplying this choice by an oscillating positive sequence preserves all frequency ratios but destroys the absolute limit.

Functional measure

Words: 29
Path integral OurBigBook.com
The functional measure is the formal integration measure over field configurations in a path integral. Its transformation under a symmetry can preserve the corresponding Ward identity or produce a quantum anomaly.
